summary: Uniswap v4 Core manages pool state in the singleton `PoolManager` and supports pool initialization, swaps, liquidity changes, donations, and token settlement. Pool actions run within an `unlock` callback, where currency deltas must be settled before the unlock ends, and initialized pools can invoke callbacks selected by their hook address.

contracts.name: PoolManager
contracts.role: Owns pool state and coordinates initialization, pool actions, hooks, and unlock settlement.

contracts.name: Pool
contracts.role: Implements pool initialization, liquidity changes, and swap state transitions.

contracts.name: Hooks
contracts.role: Validates hook permissions and dispatches callbacks for pool actions.

contracts.name: TickMath
contracts.role: Converts between ticks and square-root prices while enforcing protocol bounds.

contracts.name: Position
contracts.role: Tracks position liquidity and fees owed as positions are updated.

contracts.name: ProtocolFees
contracts.role: Manages protocol fee configuration and collection.

invariants.why: An unlock with unsettled currency deltas could leave obligations unpaid.

invariants.statement: `PoolManager.initialize` accepts a `PoolKey` only when `currency0 < currency1` and `MIN_TICK_SPACING <= tickSpacing <= MAX_TICK_SPACING`.
invariants.why: Invalid currency ordering or tick spacing can break pool identity and tick operations.

invariants.statement: `Pool.initialize` succeeds only when `slot0.sqrtPriceX96()` is zero, and the resulting price is valid for `TickMath.getTickAtSqrtPrice`.
invariants.why: Reinitialization or an invalid starting price can corrupt the pool's initial state.
Misordered or out-of-range position ticks invalidate liquidity and fee calculations.

invariants.statement: `Hooks.isValidHookAddress` rejects each return-delta permission unless its corresponding action permission is also set.
invariants.why: A pool could otherwise be configured to accept a hook delta for a callback that never runs.

invariants.statement: `TickMath.getTickAtSqrtPrice` returns a tick whose square-root price is no greater than the input price, for every accepted input price.
invariants.why: Incorrect price-to-tick ordering can make swaps cross ticks at the wrong price.

issues.title: spec: prove unlock requires all currency deltas to be settled
issues.scope: Model `PoolManager.unlock` opening the lock, running `IUnlockCallback.unlockCallback`, and checking `NonzeroDeltaCount.read()`. Prove that it relocks successfully only when the count is zero, and otherwise reverts without completing the unlock.

issues.title: spec: prove PoolKey initialization bounds and currency ordering
issues.scope: Model the validation checks in `PoolManager.initialize` for `currency0`, `currency1`, and `tickSpacing`. Prove that only ordered currencies and spacing within `MIN_TICK_SPACING` and `MAX_TICK_SPACING` reach pool initialization.

issues.title: spec: prove Pool initialization is single-use and price-bounded
issues.scope: Model `Pool.initialize` and its call to `TickMath.getTickAtSqrtPrice`. Prove that an already initialized pool cannot be initialized again and that successful initialization stores a price in the valid range with its corresponding tick.

issues.title: spec: prove liquidity tick ranges are ordered and in bounds
issues.scope: Model `Pool.checkTicks`, which is called by `Pool.modifyLiquidity` for a position's lower and upper ticks. Prove that the function accepts only `tickLower < tickUpper` with both ticks within `TickMath.MIN_TICK` and `TickMath.MAX_TICK`.

issues.title: spec: prove hook return-delta permissions require action permissions
issues.scope: Model the permission checks in `Hooks.isValidHookAddress` for before-swap, after-swap, after-add-liquidity, and after-remove-liquidity return deltas. Prove that a hook address is rejected whenever a return-delta flag is set without its corresponding action flag.

team.why: The singleton accounting, concentrated-liquidity math, and configurable hooks make this a high-stakes and intricate protocol.
